candidates.title: Reading & Northern 4-8-4 No. 2102 to make Nov. 24 appearance in Wilkes-Barre
candidates.excerpt: WILKES-BARRE, Pa. — Reading & Northern Railroad’s former Reading Co. 4-8-4, No. 2102, will make an appearance today in Wilkes-Barre to celebrate the railroad’s acquisition of rail lines that had been owned by the Luzerne County Redevelopment Authority. R&N’s purchase of the rail lines became effective on Monday, the Wilkes-Barre Times Leader reports. candidates.title: Cripplebush Valley Models rubber rock castings
candidates.excerpt: While prairie railroads and their relatively flat landscapes are simple to model, nothing rivals the dramatic look of mountain scenery. Soaring peaks, rugged outcroppings, and steep canyon walls are all hallmarks of railroading’s battle with nature at its most intense. However, building finely detailed mountain scenery can be a daunting task when using time consuming traditional methods, such as carving wet plaster or by stacking multiple small plaster castings to build larger rock walls. For a better solution, consider using rubber rock castings from Cripplebush Valley Models. This firm offers lightweight, highly detailed, ready to install rubber rock castings. They come pre-colored in sturdy, yet still flexible rubber material, allowing you to produce mountain scenery quickly and easily on your toy train layout. candidates.title: Repurposed railroad equipment
candidates.excerpt: Q: I recently saw an announcement for Athearn’s new HO scale concession cupola caboose sets. Three of the cabooses were converted to serve food (ice cream, hot dogs, and pizza) and one is decorated in a patriotic motif for the chamber of commerce. What are some other examples of repurposed railroad equipment? — Buddy C. A: Though we think of recycling as a relatively modern concept, railroads have been reusing equipment for years. Boxcars, cabooses, and passenger equipment have been converted to yard offices and maintenance-of-way storage sheds by numerous railroads. One of my favorite examples of railroad recycling is the sand tower at Wisconsin Central’s (now Canadian National’s) North Fond du Lac, Wis., yard. It was fashioned, in part, out of a modified two-bay offset-side hopper. Kazuo Terasawa shared how he modeled it in HO scale in the June 2011 issue of Model Railroader. candidates.title: STB Proposes Comprehensive Reforms to Streamline Trail Use and Railbanking Process
candidates.excerpt: For Release 11/24/2026 (Tuesday) No. 26-26 [PDF Version] Contact: (202) 245-0245 The Surface Transportation Board today issued a notice of proposed rulemaking to modernize and simplify the Board’s trail use and railbanking regulations. The proposal would reduce regulatory burdens, streamline the railbanking process, and better align the Board’s procedures with its limited, ministerial role under the National Trails System Act Amendments of 1983 (the Trails Act). Consistent with the statute, the proposed rule eliminates the Board’s role in the negotiation of interim trail use, provides a discontinuance pathway to trail use, and clarifies the Board’s role when implementing the Trails Act, among other changes. candidates.title: Maersk introduces document amendment fee in North America
candidates.excerpt: Maersk will introduce a Transport Document Amendment Fee for certain shipments loading from ports in the United States and Canada. The charge will take effect on 1 January 2027. A fee of US$75 will apply to eligible amendment requests submitted three or more calendar days after the containers have been loaded aboard the vessel at the first load port. Maersk refers to the new timeframe as the “Laden on Board + 3 Day Rule”. The fee will cover late changes to transport document details, including requests to change the document type from a negotiable Bill of Lading to a Sea Waybill or vice versa. Amendments excluded from the fee The charge will not apply to: - Seal number additions or modifications - Mandatory reference changes required for regulatory or compliance purposes - House Bill of Lading requests, amendments or cancellations - Out-of-gauge shipments Maersk noted that the fee may still apply when a single request combines an excluded amendment with other chargeable document change

candidates.title: Port of Gothenburg invests in electrified rail access
candidates.excerpt: The Port of Gothenburg is installing overhead line infrastructure on the container terminal’s handling tracks, allowing electric locomotives to run directly to and from the terminal. This removes the need for diesel locomotives or detours via the port departure yard, and is intended to raise capacity, cut emissions and make rail operations more efficient. Construction is due to begin next year. The terminal is operated by APM Terminals and handles about 80 trains a week, linking the port with more than 20 destinations across Sweden. Rail freight is growing: a record 529,000 TEU moved to and from the port by rail last year, and volumes have continued to rise in 2026. The project aims to make better use of existing infrastructure as demand increases. The investment is expected to shorten total turnaround times for container rail shuttles by up to 30 minutes, because trains can depart straight from the terminal rather than spending time in the departure yard. Adjusted EBITDA increased to US$207.3 million from US$181.6 million. Danaos’ containership segment generated US$247.8 million in operating revenue during the quarter, compared with US$239.1 million a year earlier. candidates.title: Maersk lowers Canadian inland fuel surcharge to 20%
candidates.excerpt: Maersk will reduce its Export Fuel Surcharge (EFS) and Import Fuel Surcharge (IFS) on Canadian container drayage from 24% to 20% of inland haulage. The revised surcharge will apply from 1 December 2026 and will be reviewed monthly. It covers container transportation between ocean terminals and the first inland node under both Carrier Haulage and Multi-Carrier bookings. The charge applies to the Canadian drayage portion of import and export shipments where Canada is the origin or destination. Maersk attributed the temporary measure to global energy costs and fuel availability pressures associated with the security situation in the Middle East. For non-FMC shipments, the Price Calculation Date is the estimated departure date of the first vessel shown in the latest booking confirmation. For FMC-regulated shipments, it is the date on which Maersk or one of its authorised agents takes possession of the final container listed on the transport document.

candidates.title: Port of Manzanillo gears up for expansion as box traffic grows
candidates.excerpt: Mexico’s Pacific ports race to keep pace with container growth Mexico’s chief gateways on the Pacific coast have chalked up double-digit growth this year and ... Mexico’s premier Pacific gateway is moving closer to a massive expansion after the national environmental agency gave its conditional approval for the first phase of the Puerto Nuevo Manzanillo project. This is a M$118.39bn (US$6.26bn) initiative to boost the port’s operating area from 450ha to more than 1,880ha and triple its container throughput capacity. The Secretariat of Environment and Natural Resources approved a revised proposal by Asipona Manzanillo, the port administration, after the original submission had been closed last December. Work on phase one, which should take about six years, is expected to commence in January and will see the creation of platforms for two container terminals and navigation channels. candidates.title: Maersk storms into megamax league
candidates.excerpt: Danish liner giant AP Moller-Maersk has confirmed an order for 12 ultra-large containerships of 24,000 teu, marking its entry into the largest boxship segment with an investment estimated at around $2.9bn. The Copenhagen-based group said the dual-fuel vessels would be delivered in 2030 and 2031, becoming the biggest ships in its fleet. Each vessel will be equipped with engines capable of running on conventional marine fuel or LNG, with the 12-ship series adding 288,000 teu of nominal capacity. Maersk has declined to identify the shipbuilder or disclose the contract value. Shipbuilding sources have previously put the price of the vessels at around $240m apiece. The order follows weeks of negotiations with Chinese shipbuilders, with both Hengli Heavy Industries and Hudong-Zhonghua linked to the project. candidates.title: Danaos bags $611m in fresh boxship charters
candidates.excerpt: Greek containership owner Danaos has secured another $611m in contracted revenue through a string of new fixtures and charter extensions, taking its forward revenue backlog to $5bn. The John Coustas-led company revealed the deals in its latest quarterly update, with a comparison of its fleet employment schedules showing fresh contracts for six containership newbuildings alongside longer employment for several ships already on the water. Four 5,300 teu vessels ordered at CSSC’s Huangpu Wenchong Shipyard earlier this year have secured three-year charters. The quartet, scheduled for delivery in 2028 and 2029, was previously listed without employment. Another two 9,000 teu newbuildings booked in September for delivery in early 2029 have secured charters running for at least 4.8 years. Danaos has also extended employment coverage for three of its largest containerships, the 2012-built, 13,100 teu Kota Plumbago, Kota Primrose and Kota Peony, from 2027 into 2029. US rail traffic rises 7.3% as intermodal gains 10.7% in latest week
candidates.excerpt: U.S. rail traffic rose 7.3% in the week ending November 14, 2026, compared with the same week last year, as double-digit intermodal growth outpaced gains in conventional carload shipments, according to the Association of American Railroads. Intermodal volume increased 10.7% year over year, while total carloads rose 3.3%, AAR said in a weekly update. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded gains. Motor vehicles and parts posted the strongest percentage increase among carload categories, rising 16.2%. Forest products followed with a 14% gain, while metallic ores and metals increased 10.7% and petroleum and petroleum products advanced 10.3%. The remaining categories posting increases were farm products excluding grain, and food, up 3.1%; chemicals, up 2.3%; nonmetallic minerals, up 2.1%; and coal, up 0.9%. Grain shipments fell 4.7%.
